error.message:
newspec-c: blocked → blocked (blocked)
Android rig: debug build of main e02167f bundled for the LOCAL stack only (bundle names 127.0.0.1:4510/4511, reached through adb reverse), built outside the checkout, on the rc_api36 emulator (Pixel 7, Android 16); Playwright attached to the app's own WebView; every ai/* action the app sends is answered or failed at the WebView's socket (no model call; aiCallLog had no new row in any run). Dictated words cannot be produced on the emulator (no microphone input, and the live transcription session must not be opened on the local stack), so TYPED text stood in for dictation, both contexts: text typed into the Hospital pre-round editor and the Nursing Home visit box stayed in the box and reached the server through a 30 s screen lock, 30 s in the background, an incoming call (the emulator's GSM console; it showed as a heads-up over the app) and 20 s of airplane mode (14/14 record-only checks). The airplane-mode 'no network' banner did NOT show here, but that is the rig: the app reaches the local stack through adb reverse, which airplane mode does not cut, and Android WebView keeps navigator.onLine true; with the app's socket really cut (EFS/S18 run) the banner shows. Generate with a 25 s model wait while the app sat 30 s in the background: the note was there on return in both contexts (gate TFA-92592: recorded). Left for a physical phone: real dictation through lock / background / a real call / airplane mode, and whether the words dictated before each interruption are kept.

testCase.name: [local] S20 Dictation on a real phone survives lock, background, a phone call and airplane mode (iOS and Android)

descriptionHtml:
Approach · OAT-03 Retry/Timeout Resiliency · S20 Dictation on a real phone survives lock, background, a phone call and airplane mode (iOS and Android)

UAT steps / ticket ACs covered:

  • T6 Dictation works on iOS and Android and survives a phone call, backgrounding, or a screen lock with no text lost (TFA-92570 AC 5)
  • U9 Offline / no network: a clear 'no network' message; dictation kept and retried when the connection returns, so dropped hospital Wi-Fi does not lose a physician's dictation (UAT Empty & Failure States (Offline / no network); UAT OAT-03 Source; TFA-94745 state 9)
  • U3 The physician's already-entered dictation / encounter text is preserved whether or not the note succeeded; the original input is never lost in any failure state (UAT OAT-03 step 4; UAT OAT-03 Expected Result 1; TFA-94745 AC 3; TFA-94745 state 4; TFA-94422 AC 5)
  • U13 All of the above in both Hospital and Nursing Home, on web, iOS and Android (UAT 3.3; UAT Empty & Failure States Expected Result; TFA-94745 AC 6)

Test design technique: Device (device) — Look at the layout and gestures at phone size or on a real device (iPhone / Pixel).

Given Signed builds on an iPhone (TestFlight) and an Android phone (Google internal testing). Those builds talk to the dev deployment , which is out of bounds for this runner because the store reviewers use it: owner Daniela / Tim, a @roundai.test account Tim approves, never the store-review-test-account …

When Start dictating in the Hospital pre-round and in a Nursing Home visit; mid-sentence lock the screen 30 s; background the app 30 s; take a phone call; switch on airplane mode for 20 s

Then After each interruption the text dictated before it is still in the field (and on the server once online); if dictation stopped, a clear message says so; a no-network message during airplane mode

Pass rule (oracle, excerpt): Tester compares against the script; any lost words = Fail

Where it ran: local newspec-c (new Playwright specs); test method DEVICE · Real device (iOS / Android); lane planned in the matrix: manual (manual)

S20 is our own case number (its number in the coverage matrix cases/OAT-03.matrix.json), not a step number of the UAT document.

Environment: local — main e02167f, local stack (not a deployed build); run folder runs/2026-10-14-local, lane newspec-c.

Test method: DEVICE · Real device (iOS / Android) — as classified in cases/test-methods.json, which says it runs on dev; Source: newspec-c.

UAT item: OAT-03 Retry/Timeout Resiliency · Section: B · Operational Acceptance Tests · Scenario: OAT-03/S20

Dictation on a real phone survives lock, background, a phone call and airplane mode (iOS and Android)

Tickets: TFA-92570 Mobile: Capacitor wrap for App Store & Google Play (ready for qa); TFA-94422 Haiku primary, Mistral fallback via Bedrock (ready for qa); TFA-94745 Empty & Failure States (ready for qa)

New local lane newspec-c: status blocked in newspec-c/results.json → blocked (blocked).

Detail:

Android rig: debug build of main e02167f bundled for the LOCAL stack only (bundle names 127.0.0.1:4510/4511, reached through adb reverse), built outside the checkout, on the rc_api36 emulator (Pixel 7, Android 16); Playwright attached to the app's own WebView; every ai/* action the app sends is answered or failed at the WebView's socket (no model call; aiCallLog had no new row in any run). Dictated words cannot be produced on the emulator (no microphone input, and the live transcription session must not be opened on the local stack), so TYPED text stood in for dictation, both contexts: text typed into the Hospital pre-round editor and the Nursing Home visit box stayed in the box and reached the server through a 30 s screen lock, 30 s in the background, an incoming call (the emulator's GSM console; it showed as a heads-up over the app) and 20 s of airplane mode (14/14 record-only checks). The airplane-mode 'no network' banner did NOT show here, but that is the rig: the app reaches the local stack through adb reverse, which airplane mode does not cut, and Android WebView keeps navigator.onLine true; with the app's socket really cut (EFS/S18 run) the banner shows. Generate with a 25 s model wait while the app sat 30 s in the background: the note was there on return in both contexts (gate TFA-92592: recorded). Left for a physical phone: real dictation through lock / background / a real call / airplane mode, and whether the words dictated before each interruption are kept.

Evidence: 15 attached.

Dev run: skipped: set-aside — set-aside: iOS/Android; dictation by microphone/speaker (Quinn 2026-10-14) — Set aside for the dev run (Quinn 2026-10-14: dictation by microphone or speaker, iOS and Android are set aside).. This local result replaces that dev entry (the scenario appears once).
